Re how long Is the DAT course: The American Dental Association does not have a 'classroom' class...It is a tutorial that Karina 
would do on her own...they have sample tests....a Complete DAT SAmple TEst is available for purchase from www.ADA.org. Karina 
would study at her own pace. The last paragraph says the DAT program does not endorse any test preparation course ...please see 
below from the American Dental Association web site. This is page 17 of : Dental Admission Test (DAT) 2011 Program Guide. 
Test Preparation Materials 
The DAT preparation materials contain samples of the four tests used in the DAT and are available at www.AD/korg. These materials are 
available at no charge to examinees as a means of discovering possible areas of weakness in their comprehension of subjects covered on 
the test. They also enable examinees to become familiar with the types of materials included in the test, as well as the general format of the 
various parts of the test battery. 
A complete DAT Sample Test is available for purchase. The order form with current pricing (including tax 
and shipping/handling) is available at vevetv_ADA.org.
A tutorial to familiarize you with the mechanics of taking the DAT is available at www.ADA.org. The tutorial includes a couple of sample DAT 
items, and provides the opportunity to become familiar with the basic steps involved in proceeding through the test. At the Prometric Test 
Center, you will also have an opportunity to become familiar with the workings of the computer by taking a brief optional tutorial before 
beginning the actual test. 
Additionally, you may become familiar with the computer testing experience through Prometries Test Drive. In 30 minutes, you will 
experience an overview of the testing experience you will encounter on the actual testing day. During the overview, you may participate in: 
• 
The scheduling and registration process • 
The complete check-in process • Introduction to test center staff and surroundings • A live 
15-minute sample test (generic test not a sample DAT) demonstrating the testing 
process • Full preparation for the real test 
Visit http://www.prometric.com/TestDrive/default.htm for further details and pricing. 
There are no shortcuts to the process of learning, and these test preparation materials are not designed to provide you with an opportunity to 
bypass the extensive process of absorbing basic information through class participation and months of study. 
The DAT Program does not endorse any test preparation courses and has no data on the content or efficacy of test preparation courses 
designed to prepare you to take the DAT. The DTS urges individuals considering participating in test preparation courses to review carefully 
the course materials to ensure that they reflect the current content of the DAT.

studio. 
As soon as a bike opens in the class, you can be sure we will contact you right 
away! 
Here's how it works: 
1. As bikes open up in the class, we'll give them away to riders on the wait list in 
the order that they placed themselves on the list. 
2. When a bike becomes available - bam! - you will automatically be added to the 
class! 
3. Of course, you'll get an email and a phone call as a confirmation that you are 
scheduled to ride. This can happen up until two hours before the class starts, 
so please keep in mind that if you no longer want a bike you must remove 
yourself from the wait list to avoid being charged. 
4. Please keep your phone number and email address up to date to ensure we 
are able to communicate with you. If you do not get into the class, it will be 
returned to your class series (not refunded). 
You're always welcome to come stand by for a class if you're still on the wait list as 
the class time approaches. Unclaimed reserved bikes are released 4 minutes before 
the start time for each class and are given to riders standing by in the order that they 
placed themselves on the list. There are often a number of released bikes available! 
Please note: We do not offer the option of 'switching' classes. You're welcome to 
attend a class whenever there is a bike available! However, if you're scheduled for 
one class but prefer to attend at another time, you will be charged for both 
reservations, if you have not canceled your first bike by 5 PM the night before. 
Questions or comments? Please contact 
or call

http://www.mofa.gojp/tinfo/visit/visa/short/russia_nis.html 
1) Necessary documents for "Short-Term Business Affairs, etc" 
A) Provided by visa applicant 
a) 2 visa application forms 
b) 2 photos 
c) Passport 
d) Certificate of employment 
B) Provided from Japan 
*Is there any company/organization to host Jeffrey and his assistants' visit to Japan? If not, Joi can ask one 
of Japanese companies, he has founded or invested, to arrange the following. 
a) Letter of a reason for invitation (sample on attached) 
b) Schedule of stay (sample on attached) 
c) Letter for guarantee (sample on attached) 
d) Certificate copy of corporate register or company brochure 
2) Submission 
The applicants themselves apply with all the above documents, at a Japanese Embassy or a Consulate-
General of Japan in the cities nearby. 
Ebassies & Consulates: 
http://www.mofa.gojp/about/emb_cons/over/indez.html 
EFTA00531174
--- PAGE 2 ---
*The above info is for a single entry visa. For a multiple entry visa, you have to prove you have a close 
relationship with Japanese companies, such as you are an employee of the subsidiary or something like that. 
The details for multiple visa: 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/kinfo/visit/visa/short/russia_nis.html 
*Please let me know if we need to arrange B). If so, we need the following info to fill out the letters. 
I) Each applicant's nationality, occupation, full name , date of birth and male/female 
II) Complete schedule of stay - flight info, planned activities, contact names and numbers (if available), 
accommodations on each date in Japan 
And please let me know which address (of your office) we should mail those letters to. 
*Btw, if Jeffrey is US citizen, he does't need a Japanese visa. 
http://www.mofa.go.jp/kinfo/visit/visa/short/novisa.html

Dear =, 
These panels survive for up to 20 years on the ceilings of Haus Tambaran's (structure in the Met) in the 
Washkuk. The structures have no walls, therefore the panels are somewhat exposed to the worst of the 
elements. 
The pigments are natural earth pigments which can be sealed with an acrylic matte sealer. For long term 
preservation the back side of the stripped and flattened frond should probably be treated with an 
insecticide and/or a sealer for strength. (They will be fumigated before they leave New Guinea.) 
In the Washkuk, panels are sewn together as they are never perfectly flat or the same size, nor do they 
have nails. 
I will send you a panel today. 
Best
